newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, Britain step up naval cooperation.
newsitem.headline: France, Britain step up naval cooperation.

text.p: France and Britain agreed on Friday to increase naval cooperation in areas ranging from training to arms purchases and said they hoped to conclude a similar deal next year involving their armies.

Defence ministers Charles Millon of France and Michael Portillo of Britain signed a letter of intent aboard the British destroyer HMS Liverpool, which has moored at Bordeaux during a Franco-British summit in the southwestern French port.

"This will be a very dynamic and active initiative between the two foremost European navies. It will build on the already impressive depth and range of bilateral defence cooperation which exists between Britain and France," Portillo said.
The deal focuses on maritime operations, logistical support, personnel, training and arms procurement programmes. It stops short of cooperation on nuclear submarines or joint patrols.
"We hope to follow this up with an agreement to step up cooperation between our land forces," Millon told Reuters.
Last year, the two countries set up a Franco-British air group near London to cover air force cooperation. Italy and Germany are interested in taking part as well.

France and Britain have wide-ranging military cooperation. They contributed most troops to the U.N. force in Bosnia during the war in the former Yugoslav republic and were the main European nations in the U.S.-led force in the 1991 Gulf War against Iraq.
